tools.description: Pre-delivery compliance check: does this file meet the platform's spec? Use as the last step before delivery: PASS/WARN/FAIL rows against a platform (reels, shorts, tiktok, youtube ...), each naming its fix. Writes: nothing.

max_mb.description: the caller's own maximum file size in MB: over it FAILs (the platform table's limit is guidance, WARN)

content.description: also check the content (one decode pass, plus an audio-only and a video-only one): black, frozen, silence, dropouts, flashes and first frame rows

tools.name: ffmpeg.inspect.scenes
tools.description: Find scene changes and loud moments, and propose highlight candidates so the agent can plan an edit or a digest without watching the whole file. Use to plan cuts in long footage; it can also measure a beat grid (beats), shot types (shots) and write a contact sheet (sheet). Writes: only the side files you name: edl, sheet. Relative output paths land in the output root.

input.description: Existing input file (absolute, or relative to the output root).

threshold.description: minimum scdet score for a cut, 0-100 (default 8)

ratio.description: a cut must exceed this multiple of the neighbouring frames' median score (default 3; lower = more cuts)

min_scene.description: ignore cuts closer than this in seconds (default 1)

highlights.description: number of highlight ranges to propose

rank_by.description: how to rank scenes for --highlights: audio energy (default) or scene duration

target.description: with --highlights: total seconds the picks should add up to (trims long scenes)

min_confidence.description: with --beats: below this confidence the grid is still reported, marked usable: false (default 0.5)

shots.description: label each detected shot static / pan / motion by a measured optical-flow proxy (lightweight block matching over sampled frames); reports flow_magnitude too

speech.description: report a per-second speech-vs-music energy ratio (zero-crossing-rate proxy, a measurement, not a speech/music classification)

tools.description: Cut a clip or several segments out of a video and (optionally) join them. Use to trim a clip (start, end or duration) or to keep or drop several ranges (segments, remove); lossless when keyframes allow. Writes: output. Relative output paths land in the output root.

input.description: Existing input file (absolute, or relative to the output root).

output.description: Output file with an extension; a relative path lands in the output root.

start.description: start time (seconds, mm:ss or hh:mm:ss.ms). default 0

segments.description: comma separated START-END list, e.g. '0:05-0:12,1:00-1:20' (joined in order)

remove.description: the inverse of --segments: drop these ranges and keep the rest, joined in order (e.g. '1:20-2:05,10:00-10:30'); overlapping ranges merge

smart.description: keyframe-aware cut of an H.264 source: re-encode only from each cut point to the next keyframe (and from the last keyframe to the end point), matched to the source's profile, level, pixel format, reorder depth and colour tags, and stream-copy the whole GOPs between; verified (frame grid, copied packets, decoded frames) or re-encoded in full with the...

accurate.description: always re-encode for frame-accurate (video) / sample-accurate (audio) cuts (default: lossless -c copy, re-encoding only when the keyframe snap exceeds --tolerance)

no_edit_list.description: shift the copy's timestamps instead (-avoid_negative_ts make_zero, every 2.x release's default): the picture starts at the keyframe before --start. Not with: edit_list.

no_keep_hevc.description: re-encode an SDR HEVC source with x264, as every 2.x release did (HDR still gets x265 Main10). Not with: keep_hevc.

vfr_guard.description: what keeps a variable-frame-rate source from a stream copy (default sampled since 3.0.0: re-encode only when sampled packet timestamps are variable or too few to judge; average, every 2.x release's default: a nominal rate that differs from the average re-encodes, as --accurate, and the sampled timing is reported; off: measure and keep the copy, with a note)

tools.name: ffmpeg.edit.silence
tools.description: Remove silences / dead air (jump-cut editing) or just list them. Use to tighten talking-head or podcast footage by removing pauses (and filler words with a transcript), or only to list them. output is required unless list or filler_list is given. Writes: output; side files when named: edl, timemap. Relative output paths land in the output root.

input.description: Existing input file (absolute, or relative to the output root).

output.description: Output file with an extension; a relative path lands in the output root.

threshold.description: silence level in dBFS (default -35; use -40..-45 for quiet rooms)

min_silence.description: only remove gaps at least this long in seconds (default 0.6)

margin.description: seconds of silence to keep on each side of speech (default 0.2; 0.15 before 2.22)

margin_lead.description: seconds of silence to keep before speech starts, when it should differ from --margin (default: --margin)

margin_tail.description: seconds of silence to keep after speech ends, when it should differ from --margin (default: --margin); a speaker whose last syllable trails off needs more here than before the next word

sentence_min_silence.description: for a silence after a word that ends a sentence, remove it only when it is at least this long, instead of --min-silence. Needs --words or --transcribe: a sentence end is the transcript's punctuation

sentence_margin_tail.description: for a silence after a word that ends a sentence, keep this much after the speech instead of --margin-tail. Needs --words or --transcribe

min_keep.description: drop kept pieces shorter than this (default 0.2)

speech_aware.description: keep breaths shorter than --min-silence when they sit inside a sentence (measured by re-running silence detection at a much shorter floor), and only cut at sentence-boundary pauses (--min-silence or longer). Composes with --filler through the same keep_ranges() removal list.

list.description: only print silences and the kept ranges

edl.description: Extra file to write; a relative path lands in the output root. Write the kept ranges to this file, one START-END per line

timemap.description: Extra file to write; a relative path lands in the output root. Write the source-to-output time map: every kept range with its source and output times and every removed range with the output time it was cut at; .csv for CSV, otherwise JSON (re-time subtitles, find a removed sentence again)

filler.description: also remove filler words. Needs measured word timings: pass --words or --transcribe. There is no heuristic fallback -- a word is cut only where a speech engine timed it.

filler_lang.description: which built-in list to use (default auto: the transcript's language field)

filler_words.description: Existing input file (absolute, or relative to the output root). One word per line; replaces the built-in list for this run

filler_extra.description: add words to the list. 'like', 'tipo' and 'cioè' live here rather than in the defaults: they are discourse markers, not disfluencies, and cutting them cuts real sentences.

filler_keep.description: remove words from the built-in list (e.g. --filler-keep なんか)

filler_pad.description: seconds trimmed either side of a filler word (default 0.02)

words.description: Existing input file (absolute, or relative to the output root). A whisper JSON with word-level timings, for --filler and the sentence flags

transcribe.description: produce the word timings with a local speech engine, Parakeet or whisper (never required; the same bridge caption.py uses)

engine.description: speech engine for --transcribe (default: $FFMPEG_SKILL_ASR_ENGINE, else auto = Parakeet for English speech when installed, else whisper)

model.description: speech model for --transcribe, as caption.py's: a whisper model name/path (default: $FFMPEG_SKILL_ASR_MODEL, else base), or a Parakeet model for the Parakeet engines

filler_list.description: report what --filler would remove and write nothing

max_cuts.description: refuse to render above this many removal ranges (default 400): that many cuts usually means --threshold, --min-silence or the filler list is catching speech. --list and --filler-list report them without the limit

tools.name: ffmpeg.edit.sync
tools.description: Detect the time offset between two recordings by audio cross-correlation and (optionally) write a synced output, with optional clock-drift correction.
